session_read:
Saturday, markets shut. Everything here is Friday's close, and a weekend gate is a low-information gate — no overnight session has happened for it to classify, so treat STABILIZING as an absence of evidence rather than a finding.

The book has grown to thirty-five positions and $43,736 of equity, up 12.5% in two days, drawdown healed to -2.5%. It has also, quietly, run out of money. Cash is $12.25 — 0.028% of the book against a [5,15]% band — and four buy proposals worth $1,619 were sitting open against it. That is the whole story this week. Ten names are over their own volatility-based risk caps, aggregate open risk is 14.29% against a 10% ceiling, and sentiment reads 82.9, extreme greed. A week ago I said that reading was low-volatility complacency rather than momentum, because the Nasdaq's RSI was only 63. It is 73 now. Both terms are stretched together, and the honest thing is to say the earlier caveat no longer applies.

So trimming is not a view on any of these companies. It is the only instrument that fixes both problems at once — the risk caps and the empty wallet — and extreme greed is the right tape to do it into. Six trims, about $3,280, and cash lands near 6.8%. NVIDIA reports on the twenty-sixth, confirmed, at 7.74% of the book. Going into a binary print of that size with nothing in reserve is the one thing I would not do.

Three things were wrong this week and are worth naming rather than burying. A real bug was labelling brand-new positions as stop-losses — IREN, Vertiv, Bloom, Corning all opened from zero and all got tagged as though they had been sold. Blackstone's beta was measured against the wrong benchmark and read -0.02, which made it look like a hedge; corrected, it is 1.12, and it is not one. And a sub-agent reported Coherent's quarter as an earnings miss when it was a beat with a raised outlook — the stock simply fell anyway. That last one is the same mistake as the SanDisk error a week ago, in a different agent, and the new evidence gate caught it before it moved a position. The gate working is good news. The rule not having been copied across to that agent is not, and it stays open.

The genuine improvement: this is no longer a pure single-factor book. AI-capex is 88.96% of equity, down from 93.6%, because Blackstone, Texas Instruments and a Taiwan ETF are now in it. Small, but it is the first non-AI sleeve this book has ever carried.
